title: Spin-polarized supercurrents and Josephson diode effect in altermagnets
authors: Janus F. Niebuhr, Matthias Eschrig, Danilo Nikolić
abstract: We present a systematic theoretical study of the Josephson effect in junctions consisting of a d-wave altermagnet (AM) placed between two BCS superconductors (SC). In general, the SC/AM interfaces are spin-active and modeled by spin-dependent $δ$ potentials, allowing for an arbitrary direction of the local exchange field vector. The model is formulated within the fully quantum (Gor'kov) and quasiclassical (Eilenberger) Green's function technique, applied to two distinct cases of (i) a weakly spin-polarized AM (exchange field much smaller compared to the Fermi energy) and (ii) a strongly spin-polarized AM (exchange field comparable to the Fermi energy). We apply our model to the SC/AM/SC geometry, accounting for the Josephson current-phase relation (CPR). In the weakly spin-polarized regime, the CPR displays the normal Josephson effect. Irrespective of the orientation of the altermagnet, the junction undergoes the $0-π$ transition. Depending on the orientation, the system displays the features similar to those of a ferromagnetic or an antiferromagnetic junction. To investigate the spin-polarized currents and nonreciprocal transport as the central results of the present work, we put the main focus on the strongly spin-polarized regime. Within this regime, we distinguish two cases. A coplanar exchange field profile across the junctions displays the normal Josephson effect; however, with a pure and stable long-range second harmonic in the CPR. In contrast, a noncoplanar exchange field profile gives rise to the so-called quantum geometric phases across the junction, leading to the absence of the phase-inversion center in the Josephson CPR. As a result, a Josephson diode effect emerges with a significant charge diode efficiency larger than 30% and a perfect spin diode efficiency of 100%.
summary: This theoretical study models supercurrents across junctions involving an altermagnet and superconductors. By analyzing the junction's response in different magnetic polarization regimes, the authors predict that a specific noncoplanar magnetic configuration induces a robust Josephson diode effect. This demonstrates how fundamental magnetic symmetries can govern macroscopic electronic transport properties.
main_problem: The study investigates spin-polarized supercurrents and the emergence of a Josephson diode effect (JDE) in junctions formed by an altermagnet (AM) sandwiched between two BCS superconductors (SC). The focus is on how magnetic structure dictates nonreciprocal transport.
main_result: A noncoplanar exchange field profile within the strongly spin-polarized AM regime leads to quantum geometric phases, causing a Josephson diode effect with high charge and perfect spin diode efficiencies. Conversely, other configurations yield normal or suppressed effects.
method: The analysis employs advanced quasiclassical Green's function techniques (Gor'kov/Eilenberger formalism) applied to the SC/AM/SC geometry.
model_or_system: The system is an SC/AM/SC junction where the AM is a d-wave altermagnet. The model incorporates spin-dependent delta potentials at the interfaces and analyzes transport in both weakly and strongly polarized regimes.
key_observables: Josephson current-phase relation (CPR), charge diode efficiency, spin diode efficiency, and quantum geometric phases ($\Delta\varphi$).
important_parameters: The relative strength of the exchange field ($h_0$) compared to the Fermi energy ($E_F$) and superconducting gap ($\Delta$), which defines the polarization regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes ideal SC/AM interfaces (continuity of Green's functions) and often focuses on quasiparticles at the Fermi surface. The diode effect strongly depends on achieving a half-metallic contribution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Josephson CPR for different magnetic orientations ($\phi_0$) and polarization regimes, showing how current asymmetry ($I_{ch}$ vs $\Delta\chi$) manifests as a diode effect.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the theoretical framework using Green's functions, analyzes the weak polarization limit first, and then focuses heavily on the strongly polarized regime to derive the conditions necessary for the Josephson diode effect based on magnetic field geometry.
why_interesting: This work bridges superconductivity with magnetism in a highly non-trivial way, predicting novel electronic transport phenomena (diode effects) directly controlled by the symmetry of the underlying magnetic order parameter. This is relevant for understanding superconducting spintronics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. A scheme of the system under study consisting of an altermagnet (AM) coupled to two BCS superconductors (SC). In general, the SC/AM interfaces are spin-dependent with misaligned magnetic moments. For illustration, the al- termagnet is shown in the dxy orientation (ϕ0 = π/4); how- ever, the results presented in the manuscript are obtained for the general case of an arbitrary orientation, ϕ0 ∈[0, π/4] (see the text below).

FIG. 2. The Josephson CPR in an SC/AM/SC junction for altermagnet’s thickness of d = ξ at temperature T = 0.1 Tc, different values of altermagnetic exchange field h0/∆0, and (a) the dx2−y2 orientation and (b) the dxy orientation. Panel (c): the corresponding critical currents Ic as functions of the altermagnetic exchange field h0/∆0. Panels (d) and (e): the amplitudes of the first harmonic (solid lines) and the second harmonic (dashed lines) as functions of the altermagnetic ex- change field h0/∆0 for the two orientations.

FIG. 3. The Josephson CPR in different altermagnetic junc- tions. Panel (a) shows the Josephson CPR across an alter- magnet coupled to superconductors via two spin-active in- terfaces (”trilayer”) for different misalignment between the altermangetic exchange field h and the exchange field of the right SC/AM interface JR. Panel (b) shows first four har- monic amplitudes as a function of αR. Panel (c) shows the corresponding CPR in the system featuring one interface spin active and the other normal insulating (”bilayer”). Panel (d) shows the harmonic amplitudes in the case of a trilayer (pur- ple) and a bilayer (orange).

FIG. 4. Panel (a): The charge current Ich as function of the superconducting phase difference ∆χ and the quantum geo- metric phase ∆φ. Panel (b): The corresponding spin current Isp. Horizontal cross-sections of the color scale plot from (a) taken for ∆φ = 0 and ∆φ = 0.65π [see the dotted line in panel (a)] are shown in panels (c) and (d), respectively. The currents are calculated for the ϕ0 = 0 (dx2−y2 orientation of the altermagnet), the temperature T/Tc = 0.1, and the alter- magnetic exchange field of h0/EF = 0.5. Other parameters are mentioned at the beginning of the section.

Panel (a) shows the dependence of ηch on the quantum-geometric angle ∆φ for three different orien- tations of the altermagnet given by ϕ0. Panel (b) shows the dependence of the orientation of the altermagnet for different geometric angles. Panel (c) shows the role of temperature T for different altermagnetic exchange strengths h0. Panel (d) shows the dependence on the altermagnetic exchange fields for different temperatures.
